aj: Quick RFC follow-up  idea: build a tiny "spectator" service that recommends automatic fallbacks but does not own rollout enactment. Looking for feedback on the minimal interface and failure modes.

kevin: Interesting. How is this different from the existing observer pipeline?

aj: Observer = telemetry collection & feature ingestion. Spectator = decision generator only. It writes canonical commands into a topic; the router/coordinator is responsible for applying with local checks. Design constraints: idempotent commands, TTL-based reversions, per-scope monotonicity, minimal state.

lina: Latency concern: if spectator lives in the control plane, decisions could be delayed. For very low-latency ramp downs we might need an in-runtime cache or pre-baked emergency rule.

maria: Also need auditability and reversibility. We don't want spectator to cause permanent evictions without easy rollback.

aj: Proposed flow: spectator consumes metrics (p50/p95/p99, error-rate, quality-regression signals), evaluates policies, emits events to "fallback-commands" topic. Router subscribes and applies after local capacity & mapping sanity check. Events include: scope (tenant/service), seq, idempotency_key, action, candidate, ttl_s, reason. Example: 

{"candidate":"llm-gptx-002","action":"switch","reason":"p99>350ms","scope":"tenant:doordemo","seq":42,"key":"cmd-1767901234-42","ttl_s":600}

kevin: Router should verify that applying the command won't exceed capacity or violate sticky-session requirements. If mismatch, it should either NACK with a reconcile request or query authoritative mapping.

sre-oncall: Ops wants: dry-run mode (emit only), audit log storage (default retention 90d), alert on high command churn (>10/min), and manual pin/override for SRE.

deploy-bot: Canary rolling for inference-api -> candidate llm-gptx-002 at 1% (reaction: :rocket:)

aj: On duplicate/partitioned spectator scenario: include per-scope seq monotonic field; routers ignore events with seq <= applied_seq. That avoids leader election for now.

lina: But what if spectator restarts and emits older seqs? Router should persist last_applied_seq per-scope. Also consider tombstone markers to avoid replay from long-retained topics.

maria: Per-tenant configuration: baseline_model, fallback_order (list), canary_policy (duration, ramp), churn_limits. Make fallback defaults safe: baseline first, then next-cheapest.

aj: Implementation checklist for next sprint:
1) fallback-commands event schema + examples (json)
2) router-side reconcile algorithm and seq enforcement
3) ttl + auto-rollback job behavior
4) dry-run and simulation harness to feed artificial regressions
5) observability: audit logs, metrics, alarms, and UI surface
6) runbook + SLO guidance for oncall
7) tenant policy knobs and retention settings

kevin: For reconcile: router should do a three-way compare: local mappings, authoritative mapping store, and command.expected_mapping. If any mismatch, either reject or attempt local remediation and then re-emit a reconciliation event.

sre-oncall: Add a safe-mode: if spectator disconnects for >X minutes while a canary is active, coordinator flips to baseline for affected scopes and pages. This avoids silent degradation during spectator outages.

lina: Clarify safe-mode behavior: immediate cut to baseline or gradual fallback? My vote: immediate cut to baseline to protect correctness, then allow automated graded re-enable after a reconciliation window.

maria: Also add a flag in policy: allow_spectator_autofallback = true/false per-tenant, so enterprise customers can opt out.

aj: Agree. Edge cases: spectactor vs human conflict: if human pins a model, spectator commands should be no-ops unless override flag present. Include an operator-intent header on commands ("auto" vs "manual").

kevin: To avoid thrash, add backoff semantics: when a scope flips more than N times in T minutes, escalate to manual review and freeze automated actions for that scope.

maria: Retention defaults: fallback-commands events stored 90d, audit logs 365d for enterprise compliance.

sre-oncall: We'll draft runbook snippets and alarm thresholds. Suggest pages for: spectator high-churn, spectator disconnect, command apply failures >1% for 5m.

aj: Good. I'll open a tracking issue with the checklist and link to RFC. Lina, can you draft the event schema?

lina: Yep, I'll post a PR with schema + example consumer pseudocode by EOD tomorrow.

kevin: I'll start the router reconcile patch after schema lands.

maria: I'll wire tenant config knobs into the console mockups and update docs.

sre-oncall: We'll add the runbook and SLO notifications.

aj: Thanks everyone. Actionable next steps.

kevin: :thumbsup:

maria: :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Staging deploy complete for inference-api canary (reaction: :white_check_mark:)
